context.description: The financial transactions database designed for mission critical safety and performance.

latestRelease.notes: # 0.17.9 ### Supported upgrade versions Oldest supported client version: 0.16.4 Oldest upgradable replica version: 0.17.5 ## Server * Binary: Download the zip for your OS and architecture from this page and unzip. * Docker: `docker pull ghcr.io/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle:0.17.9` * Docker (debug image): `docker pull ghcr.io/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle:0.17.9-debug` ## Clients **NOTE**: Because of package manager caching, it may take a few minutes after the release for this version to appear in the package manager. You cannot run a newer client against an older cluster: clients are only compatible with replicas from their own release *or newer*, subject to the newer release's `Oldest supported client version`. * .NET: `dotnet add package tigerbeetle --version 0.17.9` * Go: `go mod edit -require github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle-go@v0.17.9` * Java: Update the version of `com.tigerbeetle.tigerbeetle-java` in `pom.xml` to `0.17.9`. * Node.js: `npm install --save-exact tigerbeetle-node@0.17.9` * Python: `pip install tigerbeetle==0.17.9` ## Changelog ### Safety And Performance - [#3810](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3810) Revert unique keys, which caused compatibility issues (see [#3802](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3802)). - [#3822](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3822), [#3844](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3844) Extend `inspect constants` to catch schema changes and prints the `Checkpoint Schedule` section. - [#3845](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3845) Micro-optimization to the radix sort algorithm to avoid copies when dealing with large stack-allocated values. - [#3840](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3840) Online schema validation, ensuring coherent `key_min`/`key_max` when reading data. ### Features - [#3816](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3816) Improve the Ruby client migration guide. - [#3836](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3836), [#3832](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3832), [#3835](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3835), [#3834](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3834) Various docs improvements, including adding the Ruby client and print layout support. - [#3830](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3830), [#3811](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3811) Add a u128 bounds check in the Ruby client and make its status return type more idiomatic. - [#3827](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3827) Improve the Rust client, removing the bitflags dependency and enabling overflow checks. - [#3852](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3852) Experimental CLI `--memory` flag that automatically sizes the grid and object caches to use all assigned memory. ### Internals - [#3825](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3825), [#3831](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3831) Improve various code comments. - [#3793](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3793) Switch to `stdx.SocketAddress`. - [#3826](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3826) Fail on curl instead of unzip for network flakes during Vortex builds. - [#3813](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3813) Expose `TimeSim` and fixtures in VSR. - [#3820](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3820) Introduce the canonical workload principle for benchmarks. - [#3682](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3682) Make publishing TigerBeetle client artifacts idempotent. - [#3817](https://github.com/tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle/pull/3817) Workaround MacOS builds on Zig 0.14.1 (see [issue](ttps://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/issues/31658)). ### TigerTracks 🎧 - [Home](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Fc9A6mLHJU)

signals.title: ~1s commit stall once per 960 ops (checkpoint interval) under small batches on a grown data file; reproducible with tigerbeetle benchmark on stock 0.17.9
signals.text: **Summary.** On stock 0.17.9, a workload of small request batches against a grown data file stalls **all in-flight requests for ~0.7–1.6 s once every 960 operations**; the checkpoint interval (`journal_slot_count − 2 × lsm_compaction_ops` = 1024 − 64 = 960 for the release build). The slow operations form one contiguous position band immediately **before** each checkpoint trigger, consistent with the final half-bar of compaction ballooning its beat quotas. The same binary's default benchmark shape on the same machine reports its usual ms-scale latencies, because a default run (batch 8189) crosses ~1.3 checkpoint boundaries in its entire lifetime; the corner is structurally invisible to it. **One-command reproduction** (unmodified 0.17.9 release binary, single replica, one machine; ours was a GCP c3d-standard-8 with a local NVMe SSD, data file on the NVMe): ```sh # format, then grow a file with the default shape (run twice: ~38 GB, ~95–138k tx/s) ./tigerbeetle benchmark --transfer-count=10000000 ./tigerbeetle benchmark --transfer-count=10000000 # the small-batch shape against the grown file ./tigerbeetle benchmark --transfer-count=60000 --transfer-batch-count=2 \ --transfer-batch-delay=160ms --clients=32 --print-batch-timings ``` Result on our hardware: **batch p99 732 ms, p100 1,577 ms; 31 stall clusters spaced exactly 960 ops apart** (median and mean both 960); stall depth median 741 ms; 3.9% of requests > 200 ms. Single-client variants of the same shape show the same metronome at smaller depth (~55–68 ms at 19–38 GB); depth scales with file size and with how many concurrent sessions queue behind the crawl. **The mod-960 signature.** Per-request timings show the slow batches occupying one contiguous ~8–15-position band mod 960, and the band's position shifts between consecutive runs by exactly the number of ops the previous run added mod 960 (we observed 722 → 478 → 234). With `--log-debug` on our production-shaped deployment, the same interval shows per-commit compaction beats ballooning (`beat_complete` quotas in the hundreds of thousands) while the checkpoint stages themselves take 2–3 ms; the stall is a crawl across ~14 commits, not a stop. **What we ruled out.** We first found this through our application (a payments-like workload: ~2-transfer linked chains + a lookup per business transaction, 30–1,400 tx/s) and spent several rounds exonerating everything else before touching your tool: | data file on | p99 | stalls / 600 s | spacing | depth | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | shared network SSD | 818 ms | 117 | 5.13 s | 878 ms | | dedicated 450 MB/s provisioned volume | 735–994 ms | 113–119 | 5.03–5.31 s | 790–1,054 ms | | local NVMe (fio QD1 4k: 0.067 ms) | 907 ms | 111 | 5.44 s | 1,006 ms | - Identical cadence and depth across a ~100× device-latency range; - during stall seconds the device answers in ≤ 21 ms while clients wait ~1,000 ms; - TB process CPU ~15% of one core; - `--cache-grid` 1 GiB vs 16 GiB no effect on the tail; - Docker vs native release binary identical; - our client exonerated by reproducing with your benchmark tool alone. Spacing always equals 960 ÷ (prepares per second); at 31 tx/s the stall came every ~13 s, at 78 tx/s every ~5 s, and at 1,400 tx/s with deep batching it receded to one per 60+ s, which is why high-rate benchmarks don't surface it. **Why we care.** Real-money betting workload; requests are small linked chains and traffic has quiet hours, so the small-batch/low-rate corner is our steady state, and this stall is the single mechanism pinning our p99 (~1 s) at every load level. We recognize the mechanism class from the P99 CONF talk on taming TigerBeetle's tail latency and from #274's stated goal ("consistent compaction latency without write stalls"); #205 and #2942 look like earlier sightings of the same shape; #2469's fix (#2592) is already in 0.17.9 and addresses write amplification, not this cadence; #3828's full-journal direction would presumably stretch the interval but was reverted (#3841). **Questions.** 1. Is ~1 s of concentrated compaction work at the final half-bar expected at this file size, and is pacing it across the bar (or the #3828 direction) on the roadmap? 2. Is there any supported way to lengthen the checkpoint interval on a stock binary? (We understand `journal_slot_count` is compile-time and format-incompatible to change.) 3. Would `--log-debug` stage timings plus these benchmark traces be the diagnostics you'd want? We can reproduce in ~10 minutes on demand, on any storage tier, and are happy to run diagnostics or test branches.
signals.author: amogower
